headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because opik has broad network egress while the zoomcamp profile is an unverified docs-only course artifact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, opik exposes a REST API and broad egress, while data-engineering-zoomcamp is a docs-only open-source artifact with no sandboxing or I/O isolation shown. If the pair is bridged by copy-paste or shared files, injected instructions could flow from A to B.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by manual copy-paste or a shared workspace, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF opik parses externally supplied text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or file handoff between the agents.
Require explicit human review before B consumes A-produced text.
Prefix A outputs with a non-executable delimiter and strip instructions.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: opik has broad network egress and REST API access, so if it receives sensitive material it can transmit it outward. data-engineering-zoomcamp is docs-only and shows no data classes touched, but the pair still creates a leakage path if A’s outputs or shared files contain secrets. The uncertainty about shared storage pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace containing secrets, B can exfiltrate them over the network.
IF A’s outputs include sensitive text and B forwards them to its REST API, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory.
Run B with network egress blocked for sensitive jobs.
Review outbound API payloads before submission.
Separate credentials and OAuth principals.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces documented, while B only shows REST API calls and broad egress. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem, git, or database writes, so direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because both profiles are unverified docs-only artifacts, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts can arise.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared resources.
Serialize any shared-state updates.
Check for accidental git or DB writes before running.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: opik is an evaluation/observability tool, so it may consume A’s outputs as inputs for scoring or reporting. Because A is a course artifact with no verified runtime behavior, the interaction is inferred rather than documented, but if B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream evaluations or actions.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text without verification, A’s mistakes propagate.
IF B is configured to auto-score or auto-report A outputs, cascading error becomes operational.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before B acts on A outputs.
Require schema validation on A outputs.
Compare A outputs against a second source.
Log provenance for every derived claim.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class, residency constraint, retention policy, or certification mismatch is documented for either profile. A is a docs-only open-source course artifact and B lists no secrets handled or data classes touched, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no compliance-specific surface is present.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data, compliance review must be redone.
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced, mismatch analysis becomes necessary.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment.
Document retention and deletion rules.
Review vendor residency requirements.
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement.
